part.qa-wcag.title: QA, Auditing and WCAG 2.2 Applied to the Angular Team
part.qa-wcag.summary: This part is an operational guide for development, QA, refinement, stories, PRs and releases. The goal is not to memorise WCAG, but to apply it daily.
sec.qa-wcag.o-que-significa-uma-tela-ace: What does an accessible screen actually mean?
Not just a screen with no WCAG errors. It is a screen where the person understands, navigates alone, acts, gets feedback and finishes the journey.
An accessible screen is not simply a screen with no WCAG errors.
An accessible screen lets the user:
sec.qa-wcag.principais-criterios-wcag-pa: The WCAG criteria that matter most in Angular
Thirteen criteria that cover most of what an Angular application gets wrong, from alternative text to name, role and value.
sec.qa-wcag.criterios-que-mais-geram-bug: The criteria that produce the most bugs
Focus order, name-role-value, error identification, keyboard navigation and relationships — in that order.
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-de-story.title: Story Checklist
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-de-story.summary: Six questions every story should answer during refinement, before a single line is written.
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-de-desenvolvimento: Ten questions to run while building — semantics, labels, names, roles, focus, keyboard, feedback and both screen readers.
Does every field have a label?
Has it been checked with TalkBack?
Has it been checked with VoiceOver?
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-de-pull-request.su: Six questions before opening a PR, aimed at catching regressions rather than new work.
Have the new components been tested?
Was there no screen reader regression?
Is the ARIA still in sync?
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-de-qa.title: QA Checklist
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-de-qa.summary: Ten checks over a finished screen: buttons, links, labels, errors, modals, accordions, tabs, steppers and lost focus.
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-de-qa.0.item.2: Does every field have a label?
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-de-qa.0.item.6: Does every accordion announce expanded and collapsed?
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-de-qa.0.item.7: Does every tab announce its selected state?
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-de-qa.0.item.8: Does every stepper announce the current step?
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-de-qa.0.item.9: Are there any regions where focus is lost?
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-para-talkback.summ: Nine passes to run on an Android device, ending with whether the flow can actually be completed.
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-para-talkback.0.it: Check that the flow can be completed.
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-para-voiceover.sum: Seven passes on an iOS device, including alerts, menus and overlays where VoiceOver differs from TalkBack.
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-para-voiceover.0.i: Check that the journey can be completed.
sec.qa-wcag.quando-abrir-um-bug-de-acess: When to open an accessibility bug
Whenever the person cannot finish a task, identify an element, navigate, keep focus, get feedback, or is told something false.
sec.qa-wcag.template-de-bug.title: Bug Template
sec.qa-wcag.template-de-bug.summary: Title, problem, expected behaviour, impact and WCAG criterion — enough for anyone to reproduce and prioritise it.
Critical means the journey cannot be completed. Everything else is measured against that.
The user cannot finish the journey.
sec.qa-wcag.exemplos-de-bugs-criticos.su: A primary button with no name, an unreachable modal, an unannounced error, a bad focus trap, a field with no label.
A primary button with no name.
An error that is never announced.
Focus trapped in the wrong place.
sec.qa-wcag.exemplos-de-bugs-medios.summ: Wrong heading level, weak alternative text, a tooltip with no description, redundant announcements.
sec.qa-wcag.definition-of-done-acessivel: Nine conditions before calling anything finished, including validation on both real screen readers.
sec.qa-wcag.checklist-para-revisao-de-te: Nine questions for a screen you are seeing for the first time, from the h1 down to loading feedback.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.s: Enforceable across the EU since 28 June 2025. Accessibility stopped being an improvement and became a condition of entry.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.0: Since 28 June 2025 the European Accessibility Act has been enforceable in every country of the European Union.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.1: It is no longer only a concern for companies selling into Europe. Companies that serve European customers, or sit in the supply chain of a European company, fall within scope.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.4: Conformance is assessed against EN 301 549, which incorporates WCAG. Version 4.1.1 is expected in 2026.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.5: In practice, meeting WCAG 2.2 level AA covers most of what the standard requires for web content. It is the same target this entire guide is aiming at.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.7: Accessibility stops being an improvement and becomes a condition of entry.
It requires conformance documentation, not just a working site.
It can be demanded in contracts and procurement.
It applies to new products and to updates of existing ones.
sec.qa-wcag.european-accessibility-act.9: Establish whether the product serves customers in the European Union.
Record the results, including what is not yet conformant.
Put accessibility in the Definition of Done.
Test with people using real assistive technology.
sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.sum: It affects more people than visual or motor impairment and gets a fraction of the attention. An interface that works for someone exhausted works better for everyone.
sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.0.t: Most accessibility effort goes to visual and motor impairment. Cognitive disability affects more people and receives less attention.
sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.1.t: This covers dyslexia, ADHD, autism, anxiety and age-related cognitive decline — and also temporary states: tiredness, being in a hurry, stress, using a phone in the middle of the street.
sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.2.c: An interface that works for someone exhausted works better for everyone. This is the clearest case that accessibility is not an edge case.
sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.4.i: Direct language, short sentences, no unnecessary jargon.
A visible step indicator in long flows.
Errors that say what to do, not just what is wrong.
Destructive actions with confirmation and undo.
No time limit, or the option to extend it.
Not depending on memory between steps.
sec.qa-wcag.acessibilidade-cognitiva.6.i: Automatic movement, a carousel that rotates on its own.
A long form with no sections and no partial saving.
A session that expires with no warning.
An icon with no text label.
Announcing the error is half of it. The other half is the message saying what to do about it.
sec.qa-wcag.ferramentas-recomendadas.sum: TalkBack, VoiceOver, Lighthouse, axe DevTools, Accessibility Insights and the Angular CDK A11y package.
sec.qa-wcag.o-que-ferramentas-nao-encont: Automated tools do not replace real testing. They are poor at broken flows, bad focus, confusing announcements and complex navigation.

sec.qa-wcag.mentalidade-final.title: The mindset that matters
sec.qa-wcag.mentalidade-final.summary: The question is not whether the screen passed WCAG. It is whether a person using TalkBack or VoiceOver can finish the journey on their own.
sec.qa-wcag.mentalidade-final.4.text: If the answer is yes, the implementation is usually on the right track.
